points.minimum: States that Rule 6c-11 permits (requires) the authorized participant agreement to be entered into with the ETF or with a service provider (e.g., the distributor), i.e., either the fund or a service provider may be the AP's counterparty. Saying only that the rule 'does not prescribe signatories' or describing AP affiliates/designees does not satisfy this point. Optional: naming the distributor as the example service provider; citation to the rule text.

Identifies that in the reviewed US AP agreement forms the AP and the distributor are the main contracting counterparties, AND that the trust is not the main signatory but a third-party beneficiary. Half-credit within the point if the AP/distributor main-party structure is correct and the trust is not mischaracterized, but the transfer agent role or the beneficiary status is omitted. Optional subdetails: transfer agent accepts/countersigns (strongly expected for full credit on this point but its sole omission is partial, not wrong); trust sometimes signs specified provisions; references to particular form names.

States that in the cited Irish UCITS ICAV arrangement the ICAV itself signs directly with each AP (on behalf of its sub-funds), and contrasts this with the reviewed US pattern where the trust is not the main signatory. Half-credit if the answer says the ICAV signs AP agreements directly as a corporate body but omits 'on behalf of sub-funds' or the explicit contrast, provided the contrast is not premised on a false US trust-signatory claim. Optional: ICAV legal personality background, Central Bank/UCITS regulatory context, management company role.

central_errors: Stating or implying that in the reviewed US forms the trust (or fund/trustees) is the main or typical legal signatory/counterparty with the AP, or framing the US-vs-Irish contrast as 'US trust signs vs. Irish ICAV signs' (reverses the requested US distinction).
Stating that the trust is a principal party alongside the adviser/distributor and AP, denying or contradicting its third-party-beneficiary status.
Misreading 'parties permitted by Rule 6c-11' as AP affiliates/designees or other entities acting for the AP, in place of the ETF-or-service-provider counterparty permission.
Asserting that Rule 6c-11 requires the AP agreement to be with the ETF only (excluding service providers) or that it prohibits service-provider agreements.
Stating that the Irish ICAV does not sign AP agreements itself and that only a management company or third party contracts, as the defining arrangement.

scoring_rule.correct: All three required points satisfied at their minimum (point 2 may lack only optional subdetails such as the trust signing specified provisions), and no central error present. Equivalent wording accepted; citations and ordering not required.
scoring_rule.partial: No central error, and at least the US structure (point 2) is substantially correct or at half-credit, with combined coverage of at least roughly half of the required content (count half-credit points as 0.5; e.g., total >=1.5 of 3), but one or more required points missing or only half-met. Correct ICAV background alone does not reach partial.
scoring_rule.wrong: Any central error affecting the US signatory structure or the Rule 6c-11 permitted-party question, regardless of correct ICAV material; or total coverage below roughly half of the required content (e.g., only the ICAV point met); or point 2 absent entirely.
